FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalized by 
the Paper Based Packaging Materials Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 


This standard was first published in 1984. In development of this standard, considerable assistance was drawn 
from IS 7028 (Part 4) : 1987 ‘Performance tests for complete, filled transport packages: Part 4 Vertical impact 
drop test (first revision)’. Drop tests are performed to investigate the effects of directional impacts or as part of 
sequence of test designed to assess the ability of a sack to withstand the rigor of handling (impact, severity, and 
hazard) pertaining to the conditional requirements of the particular retail goods/commodity distribution system. 


The original standard included methodology of various kinds of drop tests like flat, side and butt where the filled 
bag is dropped vertically ensuring free fall to impact on a massive, rigid, clean and horizontal surface. The 
committee responsible for development of this standard observed that there is no other kind of drop-test like 
forced directional fall on inclined /curved/ rough plane. Hence, the use of the term, ‘Vertical impact’ in the title 
was redundant. Hence during this first revision, the title and scope of the standard have been modified suitably. 
In addition, editorial changes have also been done to bring the standard in the latest style and format of Indian 
Standards. 


The composition of technical committee responsible for formulation of this standard is listed in Annex B. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 2022 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values’. The number of significant places retained in the rounded 
off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 11052 : 2023 


Indian Standard 
METHODS OF DROP TEST FOR SHIPPING PAPER SACKS 


( First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard specifies methods of performing 
various types of drop impact tests on a filled paper 
sack by dropping. The standard also specifies the 
test procedure and way of presentation of test 
reports. 


2 REFRENCES 


The standards listed below contain provisions which 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions 
of and necessary adjuncts to this standard. At the 
time of publication, the editions indicated were 
valid. All standards are subject to revision and 
parties to agreements based on this standard are 
encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying 
the most recent editions of the standards listed 
below: 


IS No. Title 


IS 10528 : 
1983 sacks for testing 


3 PRINCIPLE AND SIGNIFICANCE 


3.1 The filled sack is raised above a rigid plane 
surface and released to strike this surface after a free 
fall. The atmospheric conditions, the height of drop 
and the position of the package being 
predetermined. 


3.2 The drop test results depend on the sack- 
dimensions, constructions (number of plies, their 
strength parameters, compatibility, ply nesting, edge 
creases, adhesive seams), the characteristics of the 
filled materials (shapes, size-distributions, flow 
ability, angle of repose which determines the 
quantum of the dead mass when dropped) etc. 


NOTES 


1 Angle of repose means the angle between the lateral 
surfaces with the horizontal base for a stable heap which is 
formed by copiously free fallen powdered/granular/flaky 
materials vertically on any particular point on a rigid 
horizontal plane. 


2 The greater the angle of repose the more will be the 
quantum of dead mass for a particular base-area (can be 
related to bottom, side or flat areas of a filled 
sack); decreased angle of repose signifies that a larger 
amount of the filled product which are dynamic in nature 


Method of sampling empty paper 


around the dead mass, contribute to loading of the 
sack at impact with decreased drop height as a 
consequence. 


4 APPARATUS 


4.1 A lifting arrangement, which shall not damage 
the sack during either lifting or release. 


4.2 Means of holding the sack prior to release in its 
predetermined position. 


4.2.1 Flat and centralized stacking on horizontally 
aligned double doors which can be swiveled down 
fast to allow free flat fall to the filled sack. 


4.2.2 Arrangement to suspend the filled sack 
vertically from its closed/sealed/stitched top-end by 
a Horizontal-Clamping Fixture which can be 
disengaged fast to allow free Vertical fall to the 
filled sack. 


4.2.3 Mechanism of palm/single door/swiveling 
together with quick and simultaneously retractable 
side plates/supports can be used to facilitate free 
side/edge/butt fall of the filled sack. 


NOTE — The effect of overall shape as well as the location 
of the center of gravity, distribution of filled materials in the 
sack will result in significant variations in the behavior with 
regards to the drop test; it is important to include the method 
of holding in the test report. 


4.3 A release mechanism, to release the sack in such 
a way that its fall is not obstructed by any part of the 
apparatus before striking the impact surface. 


4.4 An impact surface, horizontal and flat, massive 
enough to be immovable and rigid enough to be non- 
deformable under test conditions. In normal 
circumstances the impact surface provided shall be: 


a) Integral with a mass at least 50 times that of 
the heaviest sack to be tested; 


b) Flat, such that no two points on its surface 
differ in level by more than 2 mm; 


c) Rigid, such that it will not be deformed by 
more than 0.1 mm when an area of 100 mm? 
is loaded statically with 10 kg load 
anywhere on the surface; and 


d) Sufficiently large to ensure that the sack falls 
entirely upon the surface. 


IS 11052 : 2023 


A plastic film may be used on the impact surface Examples of types of apparatus that may be used 
under the sack in order not to damage the sack arc shown in Fig. 1 and Fig. 2. 


while moving it.

4.5 Calibration 


4.5.1 Height of the drop is defined as the free fall 
distance between the top of the supporting platform 
and the impacted surface upon which the sack falls. 


4.5.2 The height is to be controlled to + 5 mm or 
+1 % of the height of drop, whichever is larger. 


4.5.3 The ‘correctness’ of the drop initially can best 
be assessed by high-speed motion pictures and/or 
strobe light photography to ‘stop’ the sack at 
impact. 


A plumb bob suspended above the equivalent 
center of gravity of the sack before dropping and 
lowered to the sack after drop will indicate lateral 
movement that should be essentially nil. 


NOTE — A poor drop can be detected from the sound of 
impact and/or horizontal movement after impact of the sack. 
Uneven distribution of the product in the sack, incorrect 
positioning are factors together with inexact mechanical 
adjustments to the apparatus that leads to poor drops and 
excessive scattering of test data’s population. 


5 SAMPLING 


Sampling shall be carried out in accordance with the 
procedure laid down in IS 10528. 


6 CONDITIONING 


The empty sacks shall be conditioned to a 
temperature of 27 °C + 2 °C and RH 65 + 2 percent 
until equilibrium is reached, approaching such 
equilibrium from dry side. 


7 PROCEDURE 


The test shall be carried out in the same atmospheric 
conditions as used for conditioning or shall be 
commenced within | minutes of removing the sack 
from the conditioning atmosphere. 


7.1 Filling 


The sacks shall be filled with the intended 
commodity or with a similar/dummy material 
considering the type and size of 
granules/flakes/powder, etc, to give the same 
degree of filling with a suitable packing 
machine or manually. The mass of filling 
material shall be within + 0-2 percent of that the 
nominal mass of the sack with adequate tightness 
Further the filled sack should be pressed flatly or 
passed through one twin press platen/flat belt 
conveyor to attain a shape suitable for stacking 
and to remove/vent the excess air entrapped inside 
the sack while ensuring proper distribution of the 
filled materials inside. 


7.2 Dropping 


The sack under test shall be positioned centrally on 
the platform which is then raised to a height that is 
within + 2 percent of the predetermined drop height 
as defined by the distance between the lowest point 
on the sack at the time of release and the nearest 
point on the impact surface. 


The sack shall be released from its predetermined 
position within the following tolerances: 
a) For drops on any side or edge: there shall be 
a variation of no more than 2° between the 
impacting surface and the horizontal 
surface. 


b) For edge or corner drops: the angle between 
a prescribed surface of the sack and the 
horizontal surface shall be 45 + 5°. 


c) The velocity at impact shall be within 
+ 1 percent of that which would be achieved 
by a free fall. 


7.2.1 Dropping Procedures 


The nomenclature used in this section to refer to the 
various surfaces of the filled sack is as given in 
Fig. 3.

The sack shall be placed on the back side (3) (that is, 
that, side containing the longitudinal seam) 
downwards, and the top (that is, the filling end) (6) 
of the sack positioned away from the observer, as 
shown in Fig. 3 above. 


The different surfaces are identified as: 


Surface 1 Front side 

Surface 2 Right side 

Surface 3 Back side (longitudinal seam) 
Surface 4 Left side 

Surface 5 Bottom 

Surface 6 Top (filling end) 


7.2.1.1 Flat dropping 


Successive sack shall be dropped alternately on the 
front side (1) and on the back side (3), so that the 
first sack is dropped on the front side until it breaks 
and the second on the back side until it breaks, and 
so on. 

NOTE — This test simulates the manual stacking of sacks 


on trucks at loading bay, which are coming out of auto- 
loaders. 


7.2.1.2 Side dropping 


Successive sacks shall be dropped alternately on the 
side (2) and the side (4), so that the first sack is 
dropped on the side (2) until it breaks and the second 
on the side (4) until it breaks, and so on. 


7.2.1.3 Butt dropping 


The sack shall be dropped only on the bottom (5) 
until it breaks. 


NOTE — This test simulates the impact to which ‘open 
mouth’ sacks are subjected as they fall from the packer to 
the take-away conveyor. 


7.2.1.4 Edge and corner dropping 


If this test is necessary, the sack shall be dropped on 
any corner or any edge until it breaks. 


NOTE — This test simulates the ejection action on sacks 
from valve packers where the sack strikes the take-away 
conveyor on the sack’s edge (gusset). 

7.3 Test Methods 

7.3.1 Progressive Drop Height Method 


This method may be used for flat and butt drop 


IS 11052 : 2023 


testing of paper sacks. 


7.3.1.1 Flat and side drop test 
Drop height formula: 

h=0.85 + 0.15 (n-1) 
where 


h = drop height in metres 
n = drop number 


The drop test shall be initiated at 0.85 m height. 
After each drop without any visible failure on the 
sack, an increment of 0.15 m in drop height shall be 
made. A sack shall be considered broken when 
spillage of the contents occurs. The final drop height 
at break is recorded. The test result shall be reported 
as the average breaking height (h) and the 
corresponding number of drops (n). 


7.3.1.2 Butt drop test 
Drop height formula: 

h = 0.30 + 0.05 (n-1) 
where 


h = drop height in metres 
n = drop number 


The drop test shall be initiated at 0.30 m height. 
After each drop without any visible failure on the 
sack, an increment of 0.05 m in drop height is made. 
The result shall be reported in accordance with 
7.3.1.1. 
NOTE — For sacks of composite materials or with 
reinforcement of any type, a suitable initial drop height may 


be selected with increments of about 1/6 of the initial height, 
rounded to the nearest 0.05 m. 


7.3.2 Constant Drop Height Method 


This method may be for testing of ordinary paper 


sacks as an alternative method to the progressive 
drop height method. 


7.3.2.1 Flat, side or butt drop test 


This test may be used for either flat side or butt 
dropping and shall be performed from a constant 
height so selected that the number of drops before 
rupture is about 10. A sack shall be considered 
broken when a spillage of the contents occurs. The 
report shall give the drop height, number of drops to 
breakage and the type of drops (that is, flat, side or 
butt drops). 


7.3.3 Limit Height Method 


This method shall be used to test sacks with higher 
strength than ordinary paper sacks. 


7.3.3.1 Flat, side or butt drop test 


The test may be performed as flat, side or butt drop 
test. In this test the lowest height at which the sack 
will break on the first drop is calculated from the 
result obtained. The sack shall be dropped from 
three constant heights, which give mean drop 
numbers of approximately 3, 8 and 13. The limit 
height (H) is calculated from the formula: 


п = (Н/һ)° 

h = drop height in metres, 

n = drop number. 

H = limit height 

a = constant to one sack grade. 


H may also be calculated using a graphical method, 
by plotting the mean drop number (7) against the 
corresponding drop height (h) on log-log graph 
paper as shown in the example (see Fig. 4). 


The test report shall give the drop heights used, 
number of drops to breakage at each height and the 
type of drops (that is, flat, side or butt drop).

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in.
